chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Abdul Aziz ibn Zakariyya al-Lu'lu'i, from Suleyman ibn al-Mufazzal, who said: 'I heard Abu al-Jaroud narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)'
He said: 'Four things descended from Paradise: the Raziqiy grape, the Mushan date, the Imleysi pomegranate, and the Sheysqan apple.'

key_terms.الرَّازِقِيُّ: A specific variety of grape named Raziq
key_terms.الرُّطَبُ: Fresh, soft dates before they fully dry
key_terms.الشَّيْسَقَانُ: A specific variety of apple named Sheysqan

ai.seo_question: What are the four fruits that descended from Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies these four fruits as having descended from Paradise, a tradition that underscores their unique status and superior quality in Islamic cosmology. This narration is frequently cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the divine origin of earthly provisions and the continuity between the celestial and terrestrial realms.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Abdul Aziz Bin Zakariyya Al Lu’lui, from Suleyman Bin Al Mufazzal who said, 
‘I heard Abu Al-Jaroud narrating Abou Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Four descended from the Paradise – Al-Raziqy grape, and Al-Mushan date, and Al-Amleysi pomegranate, and Al-Sheysqan apple’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far from ‘Abd ‘Abd al-’Aziz ibn Zakariya al-Lu’lu’iy from Sulayman ibn al-Mufaddal who has said the following: “I heard abu al-Jarud narrate from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Four kinds of fruit came from paradise: There were grapes of al-Raziqiy, fresh dates of al-Mushan, pomegranates of al-Tmlisiy and apples of al-Shaysaqan.’”
